# RatingScale

Figma: [08k. RatingScale](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-963) · Family: 08 Safqah-Specific · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-01-01

An NPS-style 0–10 satisfaction scale - an investor taps a number to rate. The scale is coloured by sentiment zone (Detractor 0–6, Passive 7–8, Promoter 9–10) using the DS semantic colours. Composed from the RatingCell atom. RTL primary, LTR mirrored.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/rating-scale/reference.png`

### RatingScale

0 to 10 NPS question with zone-tinted cells and min/max anchors («غير محتمل إطلاقاً» / «محتمل جداً»).

Level: organism · Contains: RatingCell

Use when:
- Asking how likely the investor is to recommend Safqah
- Post-investment or post-payout feedback

Don't use when:
- For star ratings or satisfaction scales outside NPS, this is the wrong component
- For single choice text options use Radio Group

Accessibility: Radiogroup with one selection; anchors linked as descriptions.

### RatingCell

One tappable NPS value tinted by zone: Detractor 0 to 6 red, Passive 7 to 8 warning, Promoter 9 to 10 green; Selected adds a border.

Level: atom · Part of: RatingScale

Use when:
- Each 0 to 10 value inside RatingScale
- Selected state to confirm the chosen score

Don't use when:
- For generic toggles use RegionChip

Accessibility: Radio role; number is the accessible name.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

RatingScale captures “how likely are you to recommend us?” on the standard 0–10 NPS range. Each number is a tap target tinted by its sentiment zone, so the answer reads at a glance.

It replaces the old remote Rating/* colour ramp with the DS semantic scheme - error (detractor), warning (passive), success (promoter).

### Anatomy

A question, a wrapping row of 0–10 RatingCells, and min/max anchor labels.

### Parts

- Question - the prompt (“How likely are you to recommend Safqah?”).
- RatingCell - one tappable value 0–10; tinted by zone, selected = coloured border.
- Anchors - the min (“Not at all likely”) and max (“Extremely likely”) labels.

### Zones - sentiment

NPS splits the range into three zones, each a DS semantic tone:

### Detractor (0–6)

Uses bg/error-subtle + text/error; selected adds a text/error border.

### Passive (7–8)

Uses bg/warning-subtle + text/warning; selected adds a text/warning border.

### Promoter (9–10)

Uses bg/success-subtle + text/success; selected adds a text/success border.

### States - RatingCell

- Default - available but unchosen: subtle tint, coloured number, no border.
- Selected - the chosen rating: subtle tint + a coloured border in the zone tone.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

RTL (Arabic) is primary; LTR mirrors it - the number order and anchors flip so the min sits on the reading-start side.

RTL - العربية

LTR - English

### Code examples

```typescript
<RatingScale
  dir="rtl"
  question="ما مدى احتمالية أن توصي بصفقة لصديق؟"
  value={9}
  min="غير محتمل إطلاقاً"
  max="محتمل جداً"
  onChange={setScore}   // 0–10; zone derived automatically
/>
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Do

Show the full 0–10 range with min/max anchors so any score is unambiguous.

Do

Keep the sentiment colours (error/warning/success) - they encode detractor/passive/promoter at a glance.

Don’t

Don’t allow two selections - NPS is a single choice; one value at a time.

Don’t

| 3 | 7 | 10 |
| --- | --- | --- |
Don’t flatten every cell to one neutral tint - the zone colours carry the meaning.

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Zones are fixed NPS boundaries: 0–6 detractor, 7–8 passive, 9–10 promoter. Don’t re-map them.

> **Tip:** Colour comes from the DS semantic scheme (error/warning/success), not the old remote Rating/* ramp - so it restyles with the theme.

> **Warning:** Arabic (question/anchors) renders in Tajawal here - IBM Plex Sans Arabic won’t load in this plugin env; re-font before publishing. The 0–10 digits are font-neutral.
